title: Wine Wimsey Review · Mon Nov 2
subtitle: 16 feed (15 images + 1 TOBI at #6) and 4 stories for Monday Nov 2 · ISO week 45 is odd, Monday = 1 TOBI · CHARACTER: The Hot Mess (2 people-free still lifes, #4 and #11, carry the AI label) · 0 inbox items (nothing new, all 20 written fresh) · Captions: 5 SHORT, 10 SEE MORE, TOBI first comment only · EXPERIMENT: #9 (painted frost scene) and #13 (90s phone nostalgia) · FLAGS: posting date is Nov 2 because Nov 1 and Nov 1 extra already exist; no held posts

posts.quote: I sneezed in the produce aisle and my whole back sent a memo to everyone I've ever lifted anything for.
posts.caption: It was a four-out-of-ten sneeze. Nothing about it announced itself. I'm told that's how these things go.
posts.first: I once threw my back out reaching for a spice jar. The jar was fine. I moved all the spices to the bottom shelf that night and haven't looked up since. I lifted the recliner once and it took two weeks to fully forgive me.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun sneezing in a grocery produce aisle, one hand on her lower back and a wine glass in the other hand. Text in the speech bubble reads: I sneezed in the produce aisle and my whole back sent a memo to everyone I've ever lifted anything for.

posts.quote: My phone said storage was almost full. I deleted nine blurry photos of my own thumb and felt like a hero.
posts.caption: The phone gave me one gigabyte of room and I celebrated like I'd paid off a car. By 9:40 that night I'd filled it with a video of a squirrel and four pictures of a parking sign I meant to remember. The thumb photos went first, and they were not my best work. The warning came back on Thursday. I have decided to treat it as weather. I keep a folder called Maybe Delete. It has four thousand things in it and I open it every few months like a museum I'm not allowed to redecorate. The squirrel video is still in there. He is very good at his job.
posts.first: My sister once told me to just buy more storage. I said that sounded like a decision, and I'd already made one that week. She let it go, which is how I know she loves me. He's thriving. I've never deleted him.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun squinting at a smartphone while sitting on a floral sofa, a wine glass on the side table. Text in the speech bubble reads: My phone said storage was almost full. I deleted nine blurry photos of my own thumb and felt like a hero.

posts.quote: The website asked me to prove I'm not a robot by picking every square with a bus. I'd like to speak to whoever decided what counts as a bus.
posts.caption: Four rounds. The corner of a bus counted in round two and did not count in round four, and no one has explained why to me.
posts.first: I got it on the fifth try, with the motorcycle I'd skipped. I felt no triumph. The computer said welcome and I said, thanks, I guess, and closed the lid very gently. Next time I'm picking the traffic lights.
posts.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun squinting suspiciously at a laptop at a kitchen table, a wine glass in her hand. Text at the top reads: The website asked me to prove I'm not a robot by picking every square with a bus. I'd like to speak to whoever decided what counts as a bus.

posts.quote: The mail pile has a seasonal look now. I'm calling it a centerpiece.
posts.caption: Nothing in that stack is urgent, which I have confirmed by not opening it. A catalog arrived on Friday with a coupon that expired Saturday. The pumpkin was a gift and holds the pile down in a draft. Guests think it's a design choice. I've let them. I did open one envelope on Saturday, just to feel something. It was a notice that my notice was received. I put it back on the pile with some ceremony. The whole arrangement is more stable than it looks, and I'd like it to stay that way.
posts.first: Every few weeks I sort it into two piles, then put them back into one. It takes about eleven minutes and feels exactly like progress. The pumpkin supervises. The pumpkin has been there since October and no one has brought it up.
posts.alt: Still life photo of a wooden kitchen table with a tall stack of unopened mail topped with a small ceramic pumpkin, a glass of red wine, a yellow pencil and reading glasses beside it. Text at the top reads: The mail pile has a seasonal look now. I'm calling it a centerpiece.

posts.quote: I set three alarms for 6:45 and woke up at 6:44 out of spite. My body has never once respected the plan.
posts.caption: The eyes just opened. No sound, no light, nothing to fight. I lay there and listened to the alarms that hadn't gone off yet, like waiting for a train I'd already decided not to take.
posts.first: I tried going to bed an hour earlier last week. I woke up at 6:43. The body has taken a position, and I've stopped sending it memos. I made the coffee anyway, out of professionalism.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun sitting upright in bed at dawn with three alarm clocks on the nightstand and a wine glass beside them. Text in the speech bubble reads: I set three alarms for 6:45 and woke up at 6:44 out of spite. My body has never once respected the plan.

posts.quote: I've been on hold for twenty-two minutes. The music and I have started to understand each other.
posts.first: The song loops every ninety seconds, so by now I know where the saxophone comes in. A woman came on at minute nineteen to say my call was important. I believed her more than I expected to. I'm still holding.

posts.quote: I walked three blocks to save four dollars on parking. My feet charged me nine.
posts.caption: The cheap lot was behind the hardware store, past two crosswalks and one very slow man with a dog. I did the math at block two and kept walking out of principle. My feet have been billing me since Thursday. The four dollars has long since gone into a coffee. The sock-and-shoe situation happened on the way back. A pebble had gotten in somewhere around block two and I decided it was better to carry the shoe than to stop. A man in a truck slowed down to check on me. I said I was fine and meant it, mostly.
posts.first: My mother parked as close to the door as the law allowed and called it respect for her own time. I used to roll my eyes. I get it now. I get it in my arches. The truck driver was named Dale. We didn't speak again.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun walking down a city sidewalk past brick storefronts, one shoe in her hand and a paper bag under her arm. Text in the speech bubble reads: I walked three blocks to save four dollars on parking. My feet charged me nine.

posts.quote: I hit reply all today. Sixty people now know what I think of the potluck sign-up sheet.
posts.caption: I had a point. It was a fair one about the six bags of chips already signed up. But I made it in the wrong place at 2:15, with a tone I'd planned to delete. Someone replied with a thumbs-up, which I've decided to read as solidarity. The silence afterward was the loudest part. I sat there refreshing the inbox like the email might come back on its own. It didn't. I closed the laptop, took a walk around the block, and came home to eleven new messages, ten of them about chips.
posts.first: I brought a pie to the potluck anyway. Nobody mentioned the email. Three people told me the pie was good, in the careful voice you use around a thing that might go off. It was a good pie. I mention it because it was.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun at a cluttered desk staring in horror at a laptop with her hands on her cheeks, a coffee mug and wine glass beside it. Text in the speech bubble reads: I hit reply all today. Sixty people now know what I think of the potluck sign-up sheet.

posts.quote: First frost this morning. I stood on the porch in my robe and scraped the windshield with a spatula. It worked. Don't ask.
posts.caption: The scraper lives in the garage, which was a different zip code at 7:05. The spatula was on the counter, and it's flat, and it was right there. It does a better job than the real scraper and I am not looking into why. The pancakes will taste the same. I washed it first. The neighbor across the road has an actual ice scraper with a glove attached and I will say nothing against it. Mine is in the garage somewhere and the spatula was right there. The kitchen smelled like cold air and burnt toast for an hour afterward.
posts.first: The robe was my husband's idea in 2011. It has since outlived two coats and an opinion. I wore it on the porch and the neighbor waved. I waved back with the spatula. The spatula is back in the drawer. It has never looked prouder.
posts.alt: Painted illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun in a flannel robe scraping frost from a station wagon windshield with a metal spatula on a farmhouse porch at sunrise. Text at the top reads: First frost this morning. I stood on the porch in my robe and scraped the windshield with a spatula. It worked. Don't ask.

posts.quote: My dentist said floss daily. I said define daily. We both left the room feeling unheard.
posts.caption: She has the patience of a saint. I have the dental history of someone who flosses before appointments. We both know this.
posts.first: I bought a new floss pick on the way home and set it on the counter by the sink. It has been there nine days. It looks great and hasn't been asked to do anything. The dentist smiled at me with real warmth, which was worse.
posts.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun sitting in a dental chair with a bib, arms crossed and one eyebrow raised, holding a small cup of water. Text at the top reads: My dentist said floss daily. I said define daily. We both left the room feeling unheard.

posts.quote: Three of the four porch bulbs burned out in August. I've decided the house is going for mood.
posts.caption: The ladder lives behind the shed, behind the other things I haven't looked at since spring. Each bulb has gone out on a different night, so I've never had to face all three at once. The one left glows like a nightlight with ambition. Honestly, the dark corners suit the porch. The bulb in the closet drawer is the right size, I checked. The ladder is the problem, and so is the fact that the fixture is over the steps. I have done the math on how long I can run on one bulb. It's longer than you'd think.
posts.first: I did buy the bulbs. They are in a bag in the hall closet, in the same bag as the ones from last year. I took comfort in knowing where they are and left them there. My neighbor offered me a bulb and I told her I was fine. The house and I have an arrangement.
posts.alt: Still life photo of an old wooden porch at dusk with one glowing bulb, a wicker chair with a plaid blanket, a glass of red wine and a candle on a small table, red maple leaves on the floor. Text at the top reads: Three of the four porch bulbs burned out in August. I've decided the house is going for mood.

posts.quote: The quick stretch I did at 7 a.m. was a commitment. I'll be honoring it until Friday.
posts.caption: The video said ten minutes, gentle. The woman in it was twenty-six and breathing like it was nothing. I made it through the first four, then stood up too quickly and the right side of my ribs put in a formal objection. Now I turn my whole body to check the mailbox. I'm told you're supposed to do it again tomorrow to loosen things up. I'm going to let the situation resolve itself in its own time. Stairs are handled sideways for now. The dog watched the whole thing and has chosen to remain neutral.
posts.first: I did get a mat in the end. It's rolled up in the corner by the bookshelf, and it looks hopeful. I keep it there for support. I did the second half on Wednesday, in my head.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun stuck mid-stretch bent sideways in a living room with a yoga mat tangled around one foot, a wine glass on a bookshelf. Text in the speech bubble reads: The quick stretch I did at 7 a.m. was a commitment. I'll be honoring it until Friday.

posts.quote: The phones in that '90s sitcom are all stuck to the wall, and nobody ever lost one. I felt things.
posts.caption: Nine minutes into the episode I stopped following the plot and just watched the phone. Someone picked it up, talked for a while, and hung it back on the wall like a person who knew where it was. Nobody checked it. Nobody had a number to remember the number. I rewound twice. Then a laugh track came in and I realized I hadn't been laughing, just watching a phone ring and then be answered. That's a strange thing to miss. I turned the episode off and sat there with a glass of wine and the quiet.
posts.first: My parents had a yellow one in the kitchen with a cord that stretched across the room. It had a knot in the middle by 1988. I'd give a lot to untangle that knot again. It's a small thing, and it's still in the room with me.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun lying on a couch with her feet up, watching an old television with a wistful look, a wine glass in her hand and a wall phone with a curly cord behind her. Text in the speech bubble reads: The phones in that '90s sitcom are all stuck to the wall, and nobody ever lost one. I felt things.

posts.quote: The vitamin organizer has seven days on it and I've been on Thursday since Sunday.
posts.caption: Monday through Wednesday were taken care of in a burst of optimism. Then Thursday sat there looking back at me. The lid was cheerful about it, I'll give it that. I have started opening whatever compartment is closest and calling it the day. The vitamins haven't complained so far. They're very forgiving, mostly pills with good manners. The pharmacist told me once they sell the kind with alarms, and I said I'd think about it. I have thought about it, mostly in the aisle at the drugstore, holding one. It cost eleven dollars and had an alarm. I put it back and bought a candle.
posts.first: My neighbor has a lid with the letters on it and swears by it. She takes hers at 7:30 every morning. I told her that sounded lovely and I meant it. Friday is looking good, for the record.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun squinting at a seven-day pill organizer at a kitchen counter with scattered capsules, a coffee mug and a wine glass beside her. Text in the speech bubble reads: The vitamin organizer has seven days on it and I've been on Thursday since Sunday.

posts.quote: I put on a podcast to fall asleep and now I know more about medieval shipbuilding than anyone should.
posts.caption: It was supposed to be a gentle voice and a slow story. Forty minutes in I was sitting up asking the ceiling about planking techniques. I now know a ship was built with the hull first, or maybe the frame first, depending on the century and who's arguing. I did not sleep. The narrator sounded very calm. I did learn that a particular kind of oak was reserved for the keel and everyone fought about it. Somehow I remember that better than my own dentist appointment. The ceiling lamp was on until 2:30, which I'd like on the record.
posts.first: I tried a different one the next night, about gardening. It was just as interesting and I stayed up learning about compost. The ceiling doesn't say much, but I think it's learning too. The ship was finished, I think. I never learned how it ended.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun lying awake in bed at night with one earbud in and a glowing phone on her chest, a wine glass and library books on the nightstand. Text in the speech bubble reads: I put on a podcast to fall asleep and now I know more about medieval shipbuilding than anyone should.

posts.quote: My doctor asked if I exercise. I said I climb the stairs for my keys. She wrote something down.
posts.caption: It was a long answer and I stood by it. The stairs are real and so are the keys. She wrote for noticeably longer than I'd spoken.
posts.first: I've since started leaving the keys upstairs on purpose. It's the only workout plan I've ever stuck with, mostly because I keep forgetting it's one. I got my keys on the first try, which felt like a very specific prize.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun sitting on a doctor's exam table, shrugging with her arms crossed and keys dangling from one finger. Text in the speech bubble reads: My doctor asked if I exercise. I said I climb the stairs for my keys. She wrote something down.
